### Lever 3: Advertising (Targets Casual Engaged + Non-Monetized Users)

**Critical principle:** Ads only work if they're *optional and valuable* to users, not punitive.

#### **Model 1: Incentivized Ads (Video Rewards)**

**Format:**
- User encounters a limit (e.g., "You've used your 5 daily exports")
- Option: "Watch a 15-second video to unlock 1 more export today" (or similar)
- User watches video from an ad network (Google Ads, Unity Ads, AppLovin)
- Limit resets; user gets their export

**Why this works:**
- Users *choose* to watch ads in exchange for value
- No resentment; it's a clear trade
- High completion rates (40-60% typically)
- Non-intrusive; doesn't disrupt experience

**Revenue:**
- $0.50-2.00 per completed video (depends on ad network and geography)
- User watches 1-3 videos/day = $0.50-6/month per user
- 40% of Casual Engaged users watching ads = meaningful revenue without subscription

**Implementation:** 
- Show video button at moment of friction (hit limit)
- Limit video watch frequency (max 3/day) to prevent abuse and ad fatigue
- Track completion; reward only on completion, not view

---

#### **Model 2: Interstitial Banner Ads (Non-Intrusive)**

**Format:**
- Small banner ad (bottom of screen or native ad card)
- Appears between feature uses (not mid-action)
- 1-2 banners per session maximum
- Non-video, non-annoying

**Why this works:**
- Very low friction; doesn't block action
- Users tolerate if they feel app still works for them

**Why this often fails:**
- Easy to clutter experience; users uninstall
- Unless ads are *highly relevant* (e.g., sponsored products the user actually wants), they feel intrusive

**Implementation:**
- If you include banners, limit to 1 per session; rotate every 30 seconds so they fade into background
- Only use native ads (sponsored content) or ads relevant to user's use case (e.g., if app is fitness-related, show fitness product ads)
- Never use auto-playing video or sound in banners
- A/B test aggressive vs. minimal ad load; 90% of apps see churn if banner load >2/session

**Revenue:**
- $0.10-0.30 per banner impression (lower CPM than video)
- Needs scale (1M+ DAU) to be meaningful
- Not recommended as primary monetization until you've validated subscription

---

#### **Model 3: Branded Content / Partnerships (Premium)**

**Format:**
- Partner with relevant brands (non-competitive)
- Feature sponsored content/products natively in your app
- Example: Fitness app features articles/products from athletic brands; makes money via sponsorship

**Why this works:**
- Feels more like content than advertising
- Users engage more; lower churn impact

**Why it's hard:**
- Requires brand partnerships; takes months to establish
- Limited to 2-3 sponsors per quarter (or content feels overrun)
- Lower revenue than direct ads initially

**Implementation:**
- Build out subscription first; prove 100K+ paying users
- Then approach brands for sponsorships
- Start with 1-2 sponsor features/month; measure impact on retention

## SECTION IV: DETAILED IMPLEMENTATION—THE EXPERIMENT PLAN

Don't launch all at once. Run in waves, with guardrails.

### Wave 1: Subscription for Power Users Only (Weeks 1-8)

**Goal:** Prove that 8%+ of Power Users will convert to paid; refine messaging and feature set.

**Who sees the paywall:**
- Only users in the "Power User" segment (daily/near-daily usage, 6+ features, 15+ min sessions)
- Everyone else sees free, unmonitored

**How to identify Power Users:**
- Create a cohort in your analytics: "Users with 4+ sessions/week AND 15+ min avg session duration AND 6+ features used in past 30 days"
- This becomes your target segment for Wave 1

**Paywall timing:**
- Don't gate immediately; users need to build habit first
- Gate after Day 7 OR when they hit 10 feature uses (whichever later)
- Frame it not as restriction but as "unlock unlimited": "You've tried the essentials. Ready to go unlimited?"

**Paywall messaging (A/B test both):**

**Version A (Value-focused):**
> "You're using [App] daily. Upgrade to Premium for unlimited access, advanced filters, and faster support. $7.99/month, first month free."

**Version B (Habit-focused):**
> "You've created 12 projects and 50 tasks this week. Keep your momentum going with Premium—unlimited projects, team sharing, and more. $7.99/month."

**First-month incentive:**
- Free trial: First month free, then $7.99/month
- OR: Discount first month ($2.99), then $7.99/month
- A/B test both; typically, free trial converts slightly higher but has higher churn after trial ends; discount converts lower but has better retention

**Paywall placement:**
- Appears when user hits a limit (tries to create 11th project; limit is 10 for free)
- NOT intrusive; doesn't block the action, just suggests upgrade
- Can dismiss and use free tier; paywall re-appears after 3 days

**Guardrail metrics (measured daily):**

| Metric | Green Light | Yellow Light | Red Light (Kill) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Power Users uninstall rate | <1% daily | 1-2% daily | >2% daily (churn spike) |
| DAU retention (Day 1 → 7 for Power Users) | >85% | 80-85% | <80% |
| Paywall dismiss rate | <70% | 70-85% | >85% (messaging not compelling) |
| Conversion rate | >5% | 3-5% | <3% (reconsider offer) |
| App store rating | 4.2+ | 4.0-4.2 | <4.0 (stop Wave 1, investigate) |

**Success criteria to move to Wave 2:**
- ✅ Conversion rate ≥5% (ideally 7%+)
- ✅ Power User uninstall rate unchanged from pre-test (no churn spike)
- ✅ Day-7 retention of Power Users ≥85%
- ✅ App rating stable ≥4.2 stars
- ✅ $500+ MRR from Power Users alone

**If you hit red lights:**
- Stop the test immediately (remove paywall)
- Investigate: Is messaging unclear? Is the feature set not compelling enough? Did you segment incorrectly?
- Refine messaging or feature set; try again after 2-week wash-out period

**If you pass Wave 1:**
- Lock in Power User subscription (keep it running)
- Move to Wave 2

### Wave 2: High-Value Situational Users (Weeks 9-14)

**Goal:** Expand to the next segment; test usage-based pricing as alternative to subscription.

**Who sees monetization:**
- Keep Wave 1 (Power Users on subscription)
- Add: High-Value Situational users (2-3 sessions/week, 8-15 min sessions, 3-5 features)
- Dabblers and Casual Engaged still see free, no ads

**Offer High-Value Situational users a choice:**

**Option A: Subscribe ($7.99/month)**
- Same Premium tier as Power Users

**Option B: Pay-as-you-go**
- Free tier: 100 X per month (where X is your core unit: searches, exports, API calls, etc.)
- Overages: $0.02 per unit
- Monthly cap: $9.99

**Paywall timing:**
- Gate after Day 5 OR when they hit 50 usage units (whichever later)
- Allow users to switch between subscription and pay-as-you-go anytime

**Messaging (one message, choice inside):**
> "You're using [App] regularly. Choose how you want to use Premium: Subscribe for unlimited ($7.99/month), or pay only for what you use (from free to $9.99/month)."

**Expected outcome:**
- 10-15% of High-Value Situational users choose subscription (recurring value)
- 30-40% choose pay-as-you-go (they like the flexibility)
- Remaining 50-60% stay free but might upgrade during usage spikes

**Guardrail metrics:**

| Metric | Green Light | Yellow Light | Red Light |
|---|---|---|---|
| High-Value Situational uninstall rate | <1.5% daily | 1.5-2.5% daily | >2.5% daily |

**Success criteria:**

- ✅ No churn spike in this segment
- ✅ Day-7 retention ≥80%
- ✅ $1,000+ additional MRR from this segment

**If usage-based pricing underperforms:**

- Don't over-engineer; iterate fast

**If it performs well:**

### Wave 3: Casual Engaged Users + Incentivized Ads (Weeks 15-20)

**Goal:** Monetize the biggest segment (Casual Engaged) with low-friction ads; protect retention.

**Who sees ads:**
- Casual Engaged users (1-2 sessions/week, <5 min sessions, 1-2 features)
- Power Users and High-Value Situational users see NO ads (subscription benefit)
- Dabblers still see zero monetization

**Ad model:** Incentivized video ads only
- User hits limit (e.g., "You've used your 5 daily exports")
- Button appears: "Watch a video for 1 free export"
- User watches 15-30 second video; gets credit
- Limit resets after 24 hours

**Video watch frequency cap:**
- Max 3 videos per day (prevents ad fatigue)
- Video button appears after every 5-7 uses (not every time; reduces ad blindness)

**Implementation details:**
- Partner with ad network: Google Ads, Unity Ads, or AppLovin
- Revenue: $0.50-2.00 per completed video
- Set up payment terms: 70/30 split (standard for mobile apps)

**Guardrail metrics (more sensitive; ads are churn-risky):**

| Metric | Green Light | Yellow Light | Red Light (Stop) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Casual Engaged DAU retention (Day 1 → 7) | >75% | 70-75% | <70% (ad churn) |
| Casual Engaged uninstall rate | <2% daily | 2-3% daily | >3% daily (strong signal to stop) |
| App rating (overall) | 4.2+ | 4.0-4.2 | <4.0 (investigate reviews for ad complaints) |
| Video completion rate | >40% | 30-40% | <30% (low engagement; user ignoring ads) |
| Negative reviews mentioning ads | <2% of new reviews | 2-5% | >5% (stop immediately) |

**Monitoring during Wave 3 (daily check):**
- Pull uninstall rate, Day-7 retention, app rating by segment (Casual Engaged vs. others)
- If Casual Engaged uninstall rate climbs above 2.5% daily, pause ads for 1 week
- Investigate reviews; if >5% complaints about ads, immediately reduce ad frequency (cut video cap to 1-2/day)

**Success criteria:**
- ✅ Casual Engaged Day-7 retention ≥75% (baseline from pre-test)
- ✅ No spike in uninstall rate (≤2% daily)
- ✅ App rating stable ≥4.2 stars
- ✅ Video completion rate ≥40%
- ✅ $800+ additional MRR from ads

**If ads underperform:**
- Kill them immediately; revert to free-tier-only for Casual Engaged
- Focus on retention optimization instead
- Revisit ads in 6-12 months with different format

**If ads perform well:**
- Scale frequency gradually (monitor every 2 weeks)
- Never exceed 3 videos/day unless willing to accept 1-2% churn increase

**Goal:** Recover churned Power Users and High-Value Situational users; optimize retention.

**Who targets:**
- Users who churned after being Power or High-Value Situational (6+ week gap)

- A/B test free-tier UX to reduce Casual Engaged friction
- Add 1-2 high-value features to Premium tier (increase attachment)

### Step 1: Paywall Timing—Data-Driven Placement

**Rule: Gate at the moment users complete their first "core workflow," not at a calendar date.**

**Define your app's core workflow:**
- Productivity app: User creates first project + adds 3+ tasks
- News app: User completes first content search + saves 1+ article
- Fitness app: User logs first workout + views first achievement

**Reasoning:** 
- Past paywall tests often gated too early (Day 3-5), before users realized value.
- Gating after the core workflow has been completed = users have internalized value and feel loss if they can't continue.
- This is *faster* than calendar-based (some users complete workflow in 2 days; others take 9; you don't wait for the 9-day cohort).

**Implementation:**
1. Identify the core workflow completion event in your analytics
2. Create a cohort: "Users who completed [workflow]"
3. Set paywall to trigger: When user attempts action that requires workflow completion (e.g., tries to create 11th task when limit is 10)
4. Do NOT block the action immediately; show upgrade prompt
5. User can dismiss and use free tier; prompt re-appears in 72 hours

**Guardrail:** If >80% of Tier 1 users who see the paywall do so within 7 days of first session, your workflow timing is correct. If timing is spread (some in day 2, some in day 20), your workflow definition is fuzzy; clarify it.
